audited_inflection_rules.rule: Hwā/hwæt has singular morphology only. The masculine/feminine series is shared: hwā, hwæs, hwǣm, hwone; neuter hwæt, hwæs, hwǣm, hwæt. Do not invent plural or separate feminine forms. Cook also prints hwām for the dative; it is a valid recognized alternative to selected hwǣm.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Eight productive NGDA cells. Distinct hwȳ/hwon instrumentals remain reference; lexical hwȳ why is separately productive.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Use the full strong NGDA endings with each listed lexical stem: masculine singular zero/-es/-um/-ne; neuter zero/-es/-um/zero; feminine selected zero or -u/-re/-re/-e; masculine plural -e/-ra/-um/-e; neuter selected zero or -u/-ra/-um/zero or -u; feminine plural -a/-ra/-um/-a. Feminine plural -e is a valid broader strong-adjective alternative, already established in the course; the selected matrices consistently use -a. Gender/number/case still agree with the modified noun or referent.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Complete24 logical cells per selected strong model; distinct masculine/neuter singular instrumental -e is reference, not general instrumental production.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Selected feminine nominative singular and neuter nominative/accusative plural are sumu, but hwilc, hūlic, gehwilc, swilc and self. The selected ǣnig model retains -u as ǣnigu; the analogical zero-ending ǣnig is a recognized alternative. These listed outcomes govern production; a learner must not infer the entire disyllabic pattern from modern-looking spelling or from one familiar adjective.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Short sum has -u; heavy/selected zero-ending models and the explicit ǣnig alternative remain distinct. Cook and Wright state variation and analogy, so no universal spelling-only rule is asserted.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Hwæðer selects hwæðr- before the ordinary vowel endings: hwæðres, hwæðrum, hwæðre, hwæðra. Retain e before consonantal endings: hwæðerne, hwæðerre, hwæðerra. Feminine nominative singular and neuter nominative/accusative plural are hwæðer, not forms copied from prior ōðru. The earlier ōðer/ōðru paradigm retains its exact existing forms. Attested hwæðeres and simplified feminine hwæðere are valid variants; they do not replace the selected matrix.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Full strong morphology, including plural alternatives between groups. No conjunction whether or indefinite either syntax is inferred from interrogative morphology. Complete cells are model derivations, not claims of individual textual attestation.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: The selected transparent ǣnig model retains i throughout: ǣniges, ǣnigum, ǣnigne, ǣnigre, ǣnige, ǣnigra, ǣniga, and the listed ǣnigu cells. Disyllabic syncope is variable, with analogical restorations; do not mechanically contract every -ig adjective as hālig. Optional additional syncopated lexical spellings are not independently assigned here.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Full selected NGDA production. Extra dictionary text was a finding aid but its images were not obtained, so it is unused as evidence. No unsupported extra variant milestone.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Select Cook hwilc, hwæðer and hūlic. Hwelc/hwylc and expanded hwilcere/hwilcera are recorded variants. BT marks hūlīc; this is a separate source-edition spelling and does not silently change Cook's ū-only notation. Do not infer or add unprinted vowel length.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Selected-spelling recall versus acceptance of documented valid variants remains explicit.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Ilca is weak only. Its stem ilc- takes masculine nominative singular -a; feminine/neuter nominative singular and neuter accusative singular -e; other singular NGDA cells -an; plural nominative/accusative -an, genitive -ra, dative -um. Apply the same endings to self- for the weak self model; retain the separate strong self matrix.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Two complete24-cell weak systems. Weak-only ilca must not acquire an invented strong ilc paradigm. Weak instrumental is syncretic with dative and gains no general syntax here.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Ðe is invariant. The inflected relative se/sēo/ðæt reuses every prior NGDA form, alone or followed by ðe. In the selected ordinary construction, its case follows its internal role while gender/number track the antecedent; the antecedent's external case can differ. In a possessive relative, genitive marks possession within the relative clause (English whose/of whom/of which); its gender and number still refer back to the antecedent, not to the possessed noun. This uses the already productive demonstrative genitives and does not promote earlier first/second-person personal genitives or general instrumentals. Case attraction is an attested recognition exception, not assigned production.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Ordinary subject, possessive, direct-object and governed/recipient functions; relative verb person/number follows the antecedent where relevant. ðe+personal pronoun is a bounded recognition strategy.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: The recognition ge-compound uses the interrogative-type singular pattern: gehwā/gehwæt, gehwæs, gehwǣm, gehwone/gehwæt. No plural is invented.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Eight NGDA recognition cells; ordinary/partitive/distributive independent production remains Unit15. Other indefinite families have explicit dispositions.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: WeakII ætēowian keeps the lexical ætēow- stem. Present indicative ætēowie, ætēowast, ætēowað, plural ætēowiað; preterite ætēowode, ætēowodest, ætēowode, plural ætēowodon. Present subjunctive singular ætēowie/plural ætēowien; preterite singular ætēowode/plural ætēowoden. Every plural/subject-person cell is explicitly recorded. Cook allows -i-/ig(e)/g variants; exact p124 uses ætēowie without g.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Complete24-cell finite indicative/subjunctive system; infinitive/participle citation recognition only. Commands and nonfinite syntax remain unassigned. Intransitive appear is distinct from transitive ætīewan display.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: StrongI scīnan has present stem scīn- and past-plural stem scin-. Subjunctive singular/plural are scīne/scīnen and scine/scinen, for all three persons. Preserve vowel quantity; the preterite subjunctive does not use scān-.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Complete12 logical subjunctive cells; the two earlier supplied plural cells are explicitly promoted with old histories preserved.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: WeakII command endings give singular geblētsa and plural geblētsiað; preserve ge-. Previous finite indicative/subjunctive teaching did not supply this missing command pair.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Both commands productive; plain blētsian is not silently substituted for the assigned prefix lemma.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Long strong neuter līf has singular līf/līfes/līfe/līf and plural līf/līfa/līfum/līf. Plural nominative/accusative have zero ending. All earlier identities remain; ordinary countable lives and the cognate accusative with libban now justify productive plural use.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Four prior-recognition plural cells deliberately promoted, with complete eight-cell table displayed; no new abstract plural idioms.
